text:
kevin: hi all, first day! VPN reports CONNECTED but i can't hit the internal package server at 10.40.33.10 from WSL. Windows host browser can reach it, but inside WSL curl times out. anyone hit WSL weirdness during onboarding?

kevin: added some logs: on windows `route print` shows 10.40.0.0/16 -> 192.168.0.1 (my home router). inside WSL `ip route` shows 10.40.0.0/16 via 172.31.5.1 dev eth0. but curl still times out.

sophia: welcome! interesting that host can reach it but WSL can't. two common causes: (1) Docker Desktop or WSL distro created a network that overlaps 10.40/16 and Windows route/mapping is weird, or (2) WSL doesn't use the Windows VPN interface by default. which VPN client are you using?

kevin: using our-agent (wireguard backend). Docker Desktop created a subnet for containers at 10.40.40.0/24 (i just realized). could that be it?

sophia: yes — overlap between Docker network and corporate 10.40/16 is classic. Windows host likely routes traffic to the host properly via the VPN interface, but WSL has its own vEthernet translation that sends 10.40.0.0 traffic to the Docker NAT instead of the VPN. Quick test: stop Docker Desktop (`%APPDATA%\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe --shutdown`) then `curl -v http://10.40.33.10` inside WSL. If it works, that's the conflict.

kevin: stopping Docker... trying inside WSL... curl now returns 200! so it's Docker network collision.

jules: nice find. two fixes: (A) change Docker subnet (Settings > Docker Engine network settings) to something non-10.x (e.g., 172.28.0.0/16) and restart Docker, or (B) add a persistent route on Windows that forces 10.40/16 via the WG interface and ensure WSL respects it. For (B) you can run admin Powershell: `New-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix 10.40.0.0/16 -NextHop 172.31.5.1 -InterfaceAlias \"vEthernet (WG)\" -PolicyStore PersistentStore` (replace alias/gw).

sophia: small note: Docker Desktop UI doesn't always expose the subnet if using WSL backend; you may need to edit `daemon.json` or the Docker Desktop Engine JSON and set \"bip\" / fixed CIDR. If you prefer not to change Docker, (B) is less disruptive.

kevin: i'd rather change Docker subnet to avoid future surprises. where do i edit that?

jules: open Docker Desktop > Settings > Resources > Network > Docker subnet, or edit `%APPDATA%\Docker\settings.json` / Engine JSON and set \"default-address-pools\" to exclude 10.0.0.0/8. then restart Docker. we'll add a note to onboarding docs.

kevin: changed Docker to 172.28.0.0/16 and restarted. WSL `curl` to 10.40.33.10 returns 200. yay thanks!

sophia: nice. i'll add a short bullet to new-hires: \"If using Docker Desktop/WSL, avoid Docker subnets that overlap 10.40/16; change Docker default-address-pools or add a host route.\"

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-7849: \"onboarding: Docker/WSL subnet overlap with 10.40/16 causes internal access failure\" assigned to @jules. Please attach `route print`, `wsl ip route`, and Docker `daemon.json` if you hit this again.

okta-bot: Reminder: complete Okta enrollment in your default browser before starting VPN to avoid intermittent internal auth failures.

kevin: thanks everyone — saved my first pairing session. also posted the Docker subnet change in my onboarding notes. :)
